title: A Board Game RPG made with the help of AI
author: Radcroc
selftext:
Hey There!

I made a dark gothic board game RPG, inspired by games like Dokapon Kingdom, Mario Party, and Castlevania. 

Try the public playtest for free, trying to elicit some feedback and gauge interest. 

[Roll and Ruin](https://radcroc.itch.io/roll-and-ruin-prototype-playtest)

* 1-4 Local Players
* Computer-Controlled Players (AI Opponents)
* 4 Playable Classes
* Random Events and Encounters
* Relics and Character Progression
* Turn-Based Combat
* Multiple Paths and Decisions
* PvE and PvP Modes
* Controller Support

AI was used to help generate art assets and squash bugs. I have been a long-time gamedev, and AI has been an incredibly powerful tool and has helped re-ignite my passion for making games. I can actually focus on making the game rather than chasing bugs all day.

comments.author: Redditry199
comments.body: I want to ask you without trying to be extremely mean, does this not look really ugly to you? My eyes hurt from watching this.

replies.author: Radcroc
replies.body:
It does not to me.. but I’ll take that feedback.   
I am actively looking for an artist I will be the first to admit it does need a clear art direction.

replies.author: Redditry199
replies.body: I wrote a more detailed response. But that is an issue if you don't see the problem because it is not a small one. Its not about "art direction"(even though yes) its about fundamentally not understanding what art in a game is for.

replies.author: Radcroc
replies.body: Again- appreciate the feedback and more detailed notes. Always learning!

replies.author: SpegalDev
replies.body: Unless you have literal $1000s to spend on an artist, you aren't going to get one. They charge ridiculous prices for their work. Some rightfully so, most not. And one post, you'll be hounded by them for weeks/months trying to sell you their services. Good luck.

replies.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
replies.body: This is a good way to put it, lots of meaningless detail that doesn't contribute to gameplay. That's really becoming one of the hallmarks of bad AI assets.

comments.author: Fun_Score5537
comments.body: It's so difficult to read this game. All of the artwork kind of just blends together into a single mush.

replies.author: Radcroc
replies.body: Copy that. Appreciate the feedback! Something I will differently work on!

replies.author: Fun_Score5537
replies.body:
I believe in you! 

Gameplay looks solid and it's kind of amazing that you managed to create this by vibecoding. 

What's your workflow and what engine do you use? I tried something similar with Godot a year ago but I found it exhausting.

replies.author: Radcroc
replies.body:
I used to use GameMaker, but recently I've been using Godot-  
I have a background in programming; I did a lot of it myself, but I have been using Codex to clean up any systems or bugs.   
I do find Codex to be a bit exhausting on making tiny changes, but for the large pull stuff, very solid.

comments.author: lNylrak
comments.body: Hello sir may I ask how long did it take you to make this? I'm trying to set realistic expectations to my own project. Thanks in advance!

replies.author: Radcroc
replies.body: Little over 3 weeks now. But I don't really have any complicated systems or mechanics. I feel a lot of people go really big with their scope.

replies.author: lNylrak
replies.body: So what's shown in the video is everything there is? Or have you worked in like menus and stuff like that

replies.author: Radcroc
replies.body: It's actually a complete game other than the eventual online multiplayer/balancing and art, I have menus/maps/relics/multiplayer/different game modes. The video is just a small tidbit for sure.

Yeah, just a large image- Some paths take you to other "areas" (images) so I can still make larger maps as needed. I tried the 3d route and was having a lot of problems myself.   
Which genre are you working on?
